newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke - rates unlikely to change direction.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke - rates unlikely to change direction.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that German interest rates were unlikely to change direction in the near term as inflationary pressures were not expected to heat up soon.

"In light of wage developments, import, producer and consumer prices, a worsening in price perspectives is not expected in the near future," Welteke said, adding, similarly "a change in interest rate direction is also not likely."
The remarks were prepared for delivery to a group of foreign bankers in Frankfurt and were made available ahead of the speech.

Welteke, also president of the state central bank in Hesse, added these views were valid even as the economy begins recovering more strongly, a fact underscored by 1.5 percent German economic growth in the second quarter 1996 compared to the first quarter.
Welteke also said that he saw no reason for capital market interest rates to rise again in the near term.
"The Bundesbank will do its part to ensure that the stability path is not abandoned," Welteke said.

The Bundesbank most recently eased interest rates in late August when the central bank surprised international markets when it slashed its main money market rate, the repo, by 30 basis points to three percent.
Some market participants were now worried that interest rates could soon begin edging higher again, particularly as the economic recovery picks up steam.
